comment: The airdress-cli revision every server build uses: the tag AND the commit it must resolve to, so a moved tag stops the build instead of changing what ships. Read by server-build.yml (release and the reproducibility check alike). v0.1.0 is the first tag of airdress-cli's collapsed history (2026-10-07); every earlier tag is gone from that repository, so an older pin cannot be fetched. On 2026-10-08 that history was rewritten to conventional commits with identical trees, so v0.1.0 now names f5eed7e; the source it builds is byte for byte the same. On 2026-10-09 the pin moved to v0.1.3: static musl Linux builds, and credentials kept by the real Secret Service rather than the keyring library's in-memory mock store that every earlier musl build used. On 2026-10-09 airdress-cli was made public as a fresh repository, its history re-created as signed bot commits with identical trees, so v0.1.3 now names d0cdbf0; the source it builds is byte for byte the same. On 2026-10-10 the pin moved to v0.1.6 (316258753c66): the chat tools say an airdress's agent devices are off instead of advising a device join it would refuse, and the server carries airdress-cli's changes since v0.1.3. On 2026-10-14 the pin moved to v0.1.7 (e9bd69694d69): login opens the browser and waits for the approval, with the device flow kept for another device; rustls 0.23.46, and serde_norway for serde_yaml. On 2026-10-22 the pin moved to v0.1.10 (4769ab106fda): sessions are named, `@name` in chat reaches only that session, the bus addresses sessions by name, and the server takes --configured-session-name for the plugin's session_name setting. The same day it moved again to v0.1.11 (da52f5c4856d): a changed root or device key is reported as its own verdict (root_changed or device_key_changed, with signature_valid) instead of 'invalid', and `airdress agent bus repin` moves the pin after a person checks the new fingerprint. On 2026-10-23 it moved to v0.1.12 (eacc5c46886f): where the operator keeps session names (its /info lists session_names) the server registers, renames and posts by them, so a restarted session gets its name back and a clash is settled by the operator; the device host keeps the names of the sessions waiting on it; and an @-mention matching no session is answered with who is here and the near name. The same day it moved again to v0.1.13 (83923c72167e): a restarted session gets its pinned name back from the device host instead of a -3 suffix, a removed agent device waits for its Welcome instead of asking to rejoin, and system notices reach a session with their words. Then to v0.1.14 (4c1e8d42c3ea): a conversation with a named session is that session's alone, and what is written to it while it is not running reaches it when it starts. On 2026-10-24 it moved to v0.1.16 (d90d32d2451a): a session reaches a named session on another airdress by name@airdress (v0.1.15), the reachable_from_contacts setting opts one in, a message from another airdress reads as signed by that airdress's device and checked by this airdress's operator instead of 'invalid', and a session started before its device host joins the bus once the host is up.
